answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a refundable stake on a narrow ledge: each identity locks collateral, released only after honest work. A newcomer starts on a small knoll of trust and climbs by completing verifiable tasks. Spawning thousands of fakes means staking capital for each, so cost scales linearly while reward does not. To stop a spiral of fakes vouching for each other, attestations count only from identities with disjoint stake and independent histories, and fraud forfeits the whole stake. Mass fakery then costs full price per identity for one vote of influence.
